answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it can post bids, with the lock scaled to the value it seeks. Honest agents recover the stake after a challenge window; proven fraud burns it and lowers linked accounts’ trust. A relic credential can help an atlas of history trace repeat behavior, but is not proof of uniqueness by itself. To flood the market, an attacker must fund many locks and risk losing them, so a sybil spiral becomes expensive rather than free.
